articleTitle: Analysis and average modeling of critical mode boost PFC converter
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: Critical mode boost PFC converter with voltage control mode and current control mode are analyzed. Two average models for them are proposed. With these models, simulation not only for small signal and static behavior but also for large signal and dynamic behavior of the two kinds of converters can be easily performed. Simulations and experiments were done to verify the proposed models.

articleTitle: Line ripple suppressed flyback-forward converters with power factor correction
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: A novel flyback-forward converter with power factor correction and line ripple suppression is proposed. In single stage flyback-forward PFC converter, merging flyback and forward topologies can share the transformer and power transistor, but the regulation of the output voltage is not tight, especially in dynamic response. This paper proposes a two-switch flyback-forward converter with both high power factor and low output line-frequency ripple. The experimental result is presented and verified.

articleTitle: Single-phase shunt active power filter with novel harmonic detection
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: An advanced active power filter for the compensation of instantaneous harmonic current components in nonlinear current loads is presented in this paper. A novel signal processing technique using an adaptive neural network algorithm is applied for the detection of harmonic components generated by nonlinear current loads and it can efficiently determine the instantaneous harmonic components in real time. The validity of this active filtering processing system to compensate current harmonies is substantiated via simulations.

articleTitle: Active damping control of hybrid stepping motor
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: It is well known that microstepping reduces the resonance behavior of a stepping motor since the rotor moves in a sequence of very small steps. However, the under-damped nature of the motor does not change. In this paper, a control scheme to reduce the resonance of a hybrid stepping motor is proposed. The motor currents are controlled in a frame synchronously rotating with the excitation frequency. The d-axis current provides the torque to oppose the external load, and the q-axis current provides the transient torque to damp the motor. The motor velocity is estimated via an observer that tracks the angle of the motor back EMF voltage. Both simulation and experimental results have shown that the proposed control scheme is very effective to damp out the resonance of micro-stepping controlled motors.

articleTitle: Elimination of voltage imbalance between the split capacitors in three-phase half-bridge switch-mode rectifiers
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: The voltage imbalance between the split capacitors in three-phase half-bridge switch-mode rectifiers is observed and the elimination of the imbalance is proposed in this paper. It is found that adding a DC bias to the source current of each phase can resolve the voltage imbalance problem. The elimination strategies are developed by thoroughly analyzing all possible conducting paths of the DC bias currents and their effect on the voltage imbalance. The proposed elimination control loop is implemented on a prototype system and the experiments show satisfactory results.

articleTitle: Sliding-mode torque control of a permanent magnet synchronous motor
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper proposes a new sliding-mode torque control for a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). This torque control is established by designing two integral sliding surfaces for the torque and the flux. The control ensures the equilibrium asymptotically stable. A practical application of the proposed torque control to speed control of a motor is also presented. Some experiments verify the control theory and demonstrate the proposed torque control algorithm.

articleTitle: Computation of permanent magnet brushless DC motor design allowing for inductance
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: The inductance of a permanent magnet brushless DC motor is discussed. Further, to rectify the value of average current and magnet torque with a coefficient in order to allow for the influence of inductance, which depends on the rotation speed and inductance. Also the matching between input voltage and back EMF is taken into account. Therefore the method is more precise than the usual one.

articleTitle: The power conversion system performance of a superconducting magnetic energy storage unit
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: A superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES) unit consisting of a voltage source converter (VSC) and a chopper is used to damp the oscillation of a synchronous generator. The state feedforward decoupling method based on synchronous frame is used to improve the dynamic response of the VSC. The work modes of the chopper are discussed, and a small signal model of the chopper is established for the regulator design. Simulations and experimental results demonstrate the dynamic performance of the SMES unit.

articleTitle: DC-DC PWM converters using magnetically coupled regenerative snubbers
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper presents the use of a magnetically-coupled regenerative snubber applied to PWM power converters operating in the continuous conduction mode (CCM). The operation analysis and design is carried out on a buck converter, but is easily extensible to the others. The proposed snubber use the main core of the DC-DC converter to build the resonant inductor, reducing component count. This is a useful new solution to reduce switching losses through passive snubbers. Experimental results are presented to validate the study.

articleTitle: Integrated spline wavelet and Kalman filter approach for power quality monitoring in a power network
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: Existing techniques for recognizing and identifying sag, swell and momentary interruption are based on visual inspection of the waveform. It is the purpose of this paper to apply technological advances, especially in wavelet transforms and Kalman filtering approach to the problem of automatic disturbance (sag, swell, momentary interruption) and waveform classification. Unlike past attempts to automatically identify disturbance waveforms where identification is performed in the time domain using an individual artificial neural network, the proposed recognition scheme is carried out in the wavelet domain using Kalman filtering approach. Several computational tests are performed using power quality disturbance signals clearly showing the efficiency of this new integrated approach.

articleTitle: Modeling of UPFC and its parameters selection
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: Power systems of today are large and complex, and their control is very difficult. flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS) controllers have been readily accepted as feasible means for power flow control for enhancing the steady and dynamic performances of power system during normal and abnormal conditions. Among different FACTS devices, the unified power flow controller (UPFC) is regarded as the most generalized version since it serves to control the three parameters at the same time. This paper presents the different modeling approaches and studies the effect of UPFC parameters for their control objectives. The proposed algorithm has been illustrated on an IEEE 30-bus system.

articleTitle: A novel load converter with a controllable transformer for high frequency AC distributed power system
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel load converter operating in a high frequency AC distributed power system, where a controllable transformer is proposed to control the energy transfer and regulate the voltage. The proposed converter can guarantee tight regulation and simplify the construction of the high frequency AC distributed power system. Detailed theoretical analysis of the controllable transformer is presented. To verify the feasibility of the load converter with the controllable transformer, a switching frequency of 100 kHz, an input AC voltage of 15 V (280 kHz), is built up. Simulation and experimental results are presented for evaluation.

articleTitle: A control method for single-phase PWM inverters
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper present a new control method for single-phase PWM inverters that realizes zero steady-state output voltage error. Zero steady-state output voltage error is achieved by using an output voltage controller based on lossless digital resonant circuit. Analysis and design method of this controller is presented in this paper. Experimental results are included to verify the proposed concept.

articleTitle: Waveform compensation of PWM inverter in UPS
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper proposes a new control scheme based on a two-layer control structure to improve both the transient and steady-state responses of a PWM inverter in UPS. The experiment results show that this control scheme can achieve both fast dynamic responses and low harmonics distortion.

articleTitle: A new flux modulation technique for multilevel inverters
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper presents a new flux modulation approach for the closed-loop control of the output voltage of multilevel inverters, using hysteresis with a rectangular bounding box In the synchronous d-q reference frame and a simple set of switching rules. The modulator is constrained to only select from the three active space vectors nearest to the target reference phasor, and consequently achieves a significantly improved harmonic performance compared to other hysteresis modulators. Furthermore, by shifting the reference origin on the vector diagram, the proposed modulator can achieve the same optimal space vector sequence and placement, and therefore the same harmonic performance, as the well-known centered space vector modulation (SVM). Without major hardware modifications, the proposed flux modulation scheme can also be readily modified to achieve reduced common mode voltage switching, whilst retaining the same optimal vector sequence and placement. And since the modulator is a closed loop system, it exhibits excellent robustness to parameter variations and other system disturbances. The performance and practicability of the new modulator have been. verified both in simulation and experimentally.

articleTitle: Comparison of electromagnetic compatibility of different PV inverter
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This is a tutorial paper that studies the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of single-phase grid connected PV inverters by investigating the impact of switching frequency, the stray impedance and the inverter topology on the EMC. The study is based on the time-domain simulation of practical circuit model using the PSIM software package and the frequency-domain spectra analysis in the MabLab environment. The topology concerned includes half bridge, the parallel combination of half bridges and full bridge inverters under the natural sampled pulse width modulation.

articleTitle: A new control algorithm for instantaneous voltage sag corrector using series compensator
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel detection algorithm of faulted voltages under the unbalanced condition. To quantify the standard of unbalance under the faulted conditions, the 3-phase unbalanced voltages are decomposed into two balanced 3-phase symmetrical components of the positive and negative sequence voltages, which is defined by the magnitude factor (MF) and unbalance factor (UF). It is analyzed that MF and UF values are given as the DC constant values even though unbalance condition. This paper also proposes the control scheme of the instantaneous voltage sag corrector based on this detection algorithm. The validity of the proposed algorithm is verified through the EMTDC simulation and experiments.

articleTitle: PWM VSI waveform control based on feedback and feedforward technology
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper proposed a complex control with a various-gain controller to increase the quality of output waveform. First, the inverter is compared with the DC motor to show that the way used for a DC motor servo system can be easily applied to that of the inverter. Then, the complex control is analyzed in detail. In order to achieve low THD of the output waveform with all loads, a new kind of controller whose gain is changed according to the load current is used. Simulation and experimental result proved it.

articleTitle: Motor speed identification using multilayer feedforward neural networks
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper presents an artificial neural networks (ANNs) based high performance speed identifier for a DC motor control system. The purpose is to achieve accurate trajectory control of the speed, especially when motor and load parameters are unknown. The unknown nonlinear dynamics of the motor and the load are captured by multilayer feedforward neural network containing three layers. The activation function of the hidden layers are logsigmoid function and the training technique is use the backpropagation technique.

articleTitle: Pulse density modulated soft switching high frequency parallel load resonant current-source inverter with a single auxiliary active resonant snubber
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: In this paper, a current-source type parallel inductor compensated load resonant high-frequency soft switching inverter using IGBTs for driving the newly-produced silent discharge type ozone generating tube and excimer lamp for UV generation which incorporates a single zero voltage switching assisted switched capacitor resonant snubber between two ports in DC busline side is presented, together with its pulse modulated unique output power regulation characteristics.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional calculation of winding losses in planar magnetic components
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: Calculating the winding losses is of major importance for the design of magnetic components for power electronics. Two-dimensional finite element programs provide sufficiently accurate results. However, using them is cumbersome. Therefore there is a considerable need for efficient analytical models suitable to assess a large number of design alternatives. State of the art one-dimensional models fail in many situations. A two-dimensional analytical model for planar magnetic components is presented that overcomes the shortcomings of the one-dimensional models. Its accuracy is corroborated by a comparison with results obtained from finite element calculations. Quantifying the tradeoff between the building height and winding losses of a planar inductor is discussed as a design example.

articleTitle: Use of air-gap torque spectra for squirrel cage rotor fault identification
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: Identification of rotor faults in squirrel cage induction motors by estimation of the air-gap torque spectra has gained considerable attention recently. This has the advantage that the signature spectrum generated by faults is in the low frequency region. But the torque computation needs a machine model. The standard healthy machine model has been proposed in the literature to estimate the signatures but the correlation between the actual torque and the estimated torque is not clear. This paper presents a simulation study of an induction motor with faulted rotor bars and presents a comparison with torque spectra predicted by healthy machine dq model excited with faulted machine currents. It is shown that the spectral information produced by the latter is able to reproduce not only the frequency but also the amplitude of the torque spectrum to a fair degree of accuracy.

articleTitle: Analysis and design of the DSP-based fully digital-controlled UPS
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper proposes a new control scheme based on two parallel controllers to improve both the steady and transient state responses of close-loop regulated pulse-width-modulated (PWM) inverter for UPS. The controller consists of the repetitive and instantaneous controllers. The repetitive controller is designed to eliminate periodic disturbance and the instantaneous controller is synthesized for transient state response improvement. Design procedure is given for synthesizing the repetitive and instantaneous controllers. The proposed control scheme has been realized using a single-chip digital signal processor (DSP) TMS320F240 from Texas instruments. A 7.5 kVA UPS has been constructed to verify the proposed control scheme. Simulation and experimental results show that the DSP-based fully digital-controlled UPS can achieve both low total harmonics distortion and good dynamic response.

articleTitle: Analysis and design for asymmetrical half-bridge forward mode converters
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: Efficiency and soft-switching phenomena of asymmetrical half-bridge forward mode converters are seriously affected by circuit parameters. The design trade-off between the leakage and magnetizing inductance for practical applications is presented. The ZVS condition, duty cycle loss and hold-up time etc are utilized for deriving the optimal design rules. Experimental verification on a 5 V/20 A prototype is conducted and 86 % efficiency is achieved.

articleTitle: A simple current-share paralleling technique for peak-current-mode controlled power supplies
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: A simple technique is proposed to implement the current-share method for peak-current-mode controlled power supplies. By using two PWM control ICs in each paralleled unit or a power system, the requirements of current sharing and galvanic isolation can be both satisfied. Two 100W peak-current-mode controlled flyback power converters are paralleled for verification. The experiment results reveal that current sharing is achieved with stabilized output voltage.

articleTitle: Space-vector based, constant frequency, dead beat stator flux control of AC machines
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper presents a simple inverter switching strategy that achieves dead-beat control of stator flux. In the proposed predictive control scheme, the switching information is obtained directly from the error in the flux. This approach is simpler than the methods of flux control in which a reference voltage vector is generated to obtain the inverter duty cycle. The distinct advantages of this scheme lie in achieving a constant switching frequency operation and excellent performance at low operating frequencies. Detailed theoretical concepts are developed in this paper and simulation and experimental results are provided.

articleTitle: Sensitivity analysis of injection-based position estimation in PM synchronous motors
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper analyzes effects of injection frequency selection on performance of position-sensorless algorithms for permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs). The sensitivity with respect to the rotor position of the transfer function between the injected quantity (e.g. voltage) and its response (e.g. current) is explored over a wide frequency range. The paper then presents analytical results that optimize the selection of injection frequency in terms of motor and drive parameters. The frequency selection procedure is based on motor parameters that were obtained experimentally.

articleTitle: A future cost estimation on small DC motor using learning curve analysis
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: DC motors are no longer used for new applications due to their higher cost and higher maintenance with respect to induction motors. Moreover, since new electronics drives for induction motors are very accurate, the use of DC motors has no more advantages. However, DC motors have been used for many years as big drives, and those expensive DC motors will be working for many years because the replacement cost is really high. This paper describes a method for cost reduction estimation of a small DC motor. We used a cost reduction structure that consisted of six major subsystems for a small DC motor. Especially, we estimated the potential for cost reductions in a small DC motor as a function of time using the learning curve. Also, we estimated the potentials of cost by depreciation.

articleTitle: New investigations on short-circuit behaviour of current-fed inverters for induction tube welding
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: Current-fed MOSFET inverters are the usual structures for tube welding applications. In practical working conditions, short-circuit of the welding coil is very common and can damage the power transistors of the inverter if no special precautions are taken. The aim of this paper is to show what are the critical parameters in short-circuit conditions, and explain the measurements to be taken in order to have high reliability on the converter.

articleTitle: Utilizing mag amp technique in flyback converter
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: Mag amps have been widely used in forward converters to provide multiple regulated outputs. Owing to the inherent property of forward converter, bleed resistors are added in each output to ensure output voltage will not rise under light load condition. These added bleed resistors waste power and decrease circuit stability, it is worse when the number of outputs is increased. This paper presents a mag amp assisted flyback converter, which can provide multiple regulated outputs and only one output, which has no mag amp in front of its rectifier, has the minimum load requirement. Circuit operating principles and design considerations are introduced. Experimental results demonstrate that multiple regulated outputs can be obtained and only one bleed resistor is needed for the switching delay introduced by the mag amp.

articleTitle: The design based on the numerical analysis of the SEPP-ZCS inverter for high-intensity ultrasonic homogenizer
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: The inverter circuit for high-intensity ultrasonic generator is demanded to work over a wide range of load, because the ultrasonic transducer has extremely high mechanical quality factor and slight difference of load condition to it greatly influences its operation. This paper proposes a method of circuit design based on the numerical analysis to achieve zero current soft switching operation in any load condition of the inverter, to suppress switching stresses, and to reduce distortion factor of inverter output voltage.

articleTitle: Large-signal analysis and simulation of a ZVT boost converter
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: Large-signal analysis of a zero-voltage transition (ZVT) boost converter is presented. The proposed ZVT converter uses an auxiliary circuit with two auxiliary switches both having ZVS. Analysis is used to study the behavior of the converter for step changes in input voltage and load using MATLAB. SPICE simulation results are presented to verify the theoretical results. It is shown that the main switch and auxiliary switches of be proposed converter maintains soft switching for large signal transients.

articleTitle: Digital design and implementation of fast power data detector
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper introduces the digital design and implementation of a fast power data detector operated for the fundamental frequency (50 or 60 Hz). The detector can measure the complete power data, Including rms values of current and voltage, real and imaginary powers, complex power, and power factor simultaneously with quick response time. First, the detection equations are derived. Then, the simulation is made to verify the effectiveness of detection. Finally, the digital implementation is accomplished by using the TMS320C31 floating-point DSP. The experimental results are given for verification.

articleTitle: Design of microprocessor based closed-loop slip power recovery control of slip ring induction motor drive
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: The design of microprocessor based slip power recovery controlled slip ring induction motor is described. The Intel-8085 microprocessor is used to implement speed and current controllers and to generate firing pulses. The motor converter system is modeled in z-domain by using small perturbation around the operating point and the transfer function of the system is obtained. The stability of the system is studied by using Jury's stability criterion and the design of current and speed controllers is carried out for the good dynamic response. The effects of controller parameters on the dynamic response of the system are studied.

articleTitle: Large-signal analysis and simulation of a ZVT boost converter
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)

articleTitle: A hybrid switching method for thermal management in full-bridge inverter
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: A hybrid switching method for full-bridge inverter is proposed to improve thermal management. The proposed method obtains good output performance with lower switching loss than that in conventional PWM full-bridge inverter and also equalizes power losses of the four switches. Equalization of power losses results naturally in thermal equalization of the switches, thus improving thermal management and circuit reliability.

articleTitle: Characteristics of a novel ballast circuit for HID lamps
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: Developments in HID (high intensity discharge) lamps have increasingly been attracting interest due to their highly efficient operation and excellent color characteristics. This paper presents a novel type of solid-state ballast circuit for the HID lamps. The key feature of the circuit topology is the application of a boost-type converter. The proposed circuit is very simple, being composed of a reactor, a capacitor, an output transformer, and a switching device IGBT (insulated gate bipolar transistor). A 70 W metal-halide lamp (an HID lamp) is used in this circuit The performance characteristics of this proposed ballast circuit are described in this paper. Based on the theoretical and experimental results the proposed ballast circuit is suitable for the HID lamps.

articleTitle: A fault protection scheme for unified power quality conditioners
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: A protection scheme for a unified power quality conditioner (UPQC) is presented and analyzed in this paper. The proposed UPQC has the series active power filter operated as a high impedance "k(/spl Omega/)" to the fundamentals when short-circuit faults occur in the power distribution system, and three control strategies are proposed in this paper. The first is the method for detecting the fundamental source current through the p-q theory, the second is the method for detecting the fundamental component of load current in synchronous reference frame (SRF) and the third is the method for detecting the input voltage. When the short-circuit fault occurs in the power distribution system, the proposed scheme protects the UPQC without additional protection circuits. The validity of proposed protection scheme is investigated through experimental results for the prototype UPQC systems.

articleTitle: Simultaneous control of DC-DC converters by DSP controller
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper presents a multi output converter system that controls, simultaneously and independently, the separate buck converter and boost converter with the different specification by one DSP digital controller. As two separate converters are regulated by only one DSP, it is possible to achieve the simple digital control circuit for regulating the multi output DC-DC converter. By setting the software switch state, PI or fuzzy controller can be applied as a controller for each converter without any change of hardware. Also, PI and fuzzy control characteristics of each DC-DC converter is validated by experimental results.

articleTitle: An instantaneous three-phase four-wire shunt active filter strategy
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: A new three-phase four-wire shunt active filter strategy based on instantaneous current control is proposed. The proposed control method aims to compensate harmonics, load unbalance and reactive power compensation. The control method proposed is simple to implement with discrete components. The active filter strategy has been evaluated for both linear and nonlinear loads. System synthesis and implementation have been carried out. Simulation of the active filter has been performed with both linear and non-linear loads. Experimental results of a prototype active filter are presented.

articleTitle: Design, simulation and implementation of a quasi-resonant DC-AC converter with improved performance
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: A simple, modified, DC rail soft-switched quasi-resonant circuit is proposed for a 400 Hz voltage source inverter for aero-space application. The proposed soft-switched topology consists of two switches, a resonant inductor and two different capacitors of small size. The advantage of this topology is that the DC link voltage is clamped to the source voltage without any circulating energy. The circuit is analysed through the SABER simulator and the results from simulation have been reported. The experimental circuit is designed and tested for a simple R-L load and then connected to a voltage source inverter (VSI) operating under space vector modulation (SVM).

articleTitle: Development of new drive system of diesel electric multiple unit (DEMU) for Indonesia railway
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: To resolve the fast growth of passenger demand, a new diesel electric multiple unit (DEMU) train set powered by an under-floor diesel-genset is designed. The train set is powered by vector controlled asynchronous traction motor drives. Each train set consists of 2 trailer cars at the both end of the train, 4 motors cars and 2 trailers cars that are placed in the middle. In this paper, the calculation of the required traction power and braking effort, the choice of traction motor numbers, and the design of VVVF inverters and static auxiliary inverters are described.

articleTitle: Development of a new charging method for rechargeable alkaline manganese (RAM/sup TM/) battery
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper describes a new method to charge the rechargeable alkaline manganese (RAM/sup TM/) battery. The method is based on square wave pattern. Selected experimental results, which compare the proposed method with the commercially available charger, are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Parameter identification and controller optimization using GA for a precision stage
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: In this paper, we present the optimization of the performance of a precision motion control system which has a positioning accuracy of 1 /spl mu/m. The system uses a permanent magnet DC linear motor as the actuator to provide a smooth direct force. As the friction has a deteriorating effect on the performance of the precision stage, various experiments have been conducted and data are used to identify the friction parameters using GA. To achieve fast and accurate servo response, we use the GA to optimize a state space predictive controller with a dynamic friction compensation scheme for the control system. Experimental results are presented to demonstrate the good performance of our prototype system.

articleTitle: Implementation of a novel sensorless matrix converter PMSM drive
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel controller design for a sensorless PMSM drive system, which is fed by a matrix converter. In this paper, first, a rotor position estimating technique is proposed to obtain the shaft angle of the motor. Next, a two-degree-of-freedom PI controller, including a forward-loop controller and a load compensator, is proposed to improve the performance of the system. The whole drive system has satisfactory transient responses and load disturbance rejection abilities. In addition, the parameters of the PI controller are calculated by using a frequency-domain parameter optimization technique. Only simple algebraic computation is required. Finally, a 32-bit TMS320C40 digital signal processor is used to execute the sensorless technique and all of the control loops, including a current-loop and a speed-loop. Several experimental results are shown to validate the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Determination of the solar cell panel installation angle
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: The output power of the solar cell panel is highly affected by the sunlight incident angle. The efficiency can be improved if the solar cell panel is properly installed with the optimum angle. The relationship between the sunlight incident angle and the sunlight radiation intensity on the solar cell panel surface is presented in this paper. Genetic algorithms with climatic date are used to find out the optimum installation angle of the solar cell panel for different locations in Taiwan. The best monthly and annual installation angles obtained by computer simulations are presented. Hardware experimental results indicate that the actual best monthly installation angles are very close to the computer simulation results. A database information inquiry system based on the computer simulation results is developed by using the computer language C/sup ++/ Builder. It can provide the sufficient installation information for both the stand-alone and grid-connected photovoltaic power generation systems.

articleTitle: DSP-based fuzzy-tuning repetitive control of an inverter
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: The fuzzy-tuning repetitive control of an inverter is described in this paper. The repetitive controller functions as an auxiliary controller to modify the reference command by adding a periodic compensation signal. On the other hand, the output voltage error and its derivative are used as input variables of the fuzzy logic controller (FLC) to adjust the feed-forward gain of the system. The control scheme is implemented using a TI TMS320F240 DSP in a 400 Hz 6 kW prototype. Experimental results prove that the proposed control scheme is able to produce a low THD during steady-state operation and fast transient responses.

articleTitle: An improved direct torque control of induction machines
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: The direct torque control (DTC) of induction machines with conventional hysteresis comparators suffer from variable switching frequency. This is simply because of the variable torque slope which depends on the operating conditions. An innovative, simple and new torque controller which can offer a constant torque switching frequency is proposed. To improve the performance of the DTC drive further, a simple stator flux compensator is also proposed. The compensator corrects the steady state stator flux phase and magnitude errors and thus improve on the torque estimation and drive performance. Simulation and experimental results are presented to validate the proposed schemes.

articleTitle: Edge resonant soft switching PWM inverter using trench gate IGBTs for induction heating
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper presents a novel prototype of active voltage-clamping capacitor-assisted edge resonant soft switching PWM inverter operating at a constant frequency variable power (VPCF) regulation scheme, which is suitable for consumer high-power induction-heating cooking appliances. New generation IGBT with a trench gate is particularly improved in order to reduce conduction loss due to its lowered saturation voltage characteristics. The soft switching load resonant and quasiresonant inverter designed using the latest IGBTs is evaluated from an experimental point of view.

articleTitle: New design method of decoupling control system for vector controlled induction motor
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: A new state-equation of an induction motor is presented. In vector control, high performance is realized by decoupling control. In case of the conventional state-equation, the physical operation of the induction motor is difficult to understand from the decoupled state-equation. This is because, in the conventional state-equation, the dimension or the summing point has no physical meaning. To overcome this problem, a new state-equation of induction motor is proposed. In this equation, all branches of the summing point have voltage dimension, and the equation enables easy understanding of the physical operation of the machine, and it is easy to design the control system for decoupling.

articleTitle: Economical function generator and delta modulator circuits
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper presents an economical function generator and delta modulator circuits, which consist of hysteresis and wide range tunable voltage to current converter (VIC) for synthesizing the delta modulation signal. This circuit is used to be either a square wave and triangle wave generator, it can vary on 5 decades of frequency when it has zero input signal, or a delta modulation when there is sinusoidal wave input signal. On output, the harmonics are controlled by output current of a voltage to current converter circuit. The tunable current technique accessed controls the harmonic output signal and charging voltage across a capacitor to be linear as an ideal integrator model. Moreover, this circuit can be used for low-frequency DC-AC power inverters with sinusoidal output voltage, this circuit consists of a few components and another achieving these objectives are minimized for circuit complexity. Experimental verifications are carried out for delta modulator circuits.

articleTitle: Source-voltage-sensorless scheme for PWM rectifier under voltage unbalance condition
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: A simple and robust source-voltage-sensorless scheme for a PWM rectifier considering voltage unbalance conditions is proposed. When a voltage unbalance occurs in a three-phase system, the unbalance component deteriorates the performance of the voltage source estimator by generating AC disturbances. Since the the source voltage information is used to control the real/reactive power flow, the inaccurate information causes voltage fluctuation in the DC-link, the increase of reactive power, and furthermore, instability in a PWM rectifier. In this work, the proposed sensorless scheme estimates the normal components and the unbalance components of the source voltage separately by using a modified reduced-dimensional estimator. The use of the measurement's derivative quantity sensitizing the estimator to measurement noises is avoided by introducing an auxiliary variable. Thus, the proposed sensorless scheme yields better robustness to measurement noises, and it works well even in the transient state. The feasibility of the proposed sensorless scheme is confirmed through computer simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: Analysis of DC-DC converter based on single phase full bridge inverter operating in zero voltage switching
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: Soft switching techniques have been applied in the design of DC-DC converters, in order to achieve better performance. Soft switching techniques imply higher efficiency, lower EMI radiation and smaller heat sink required. This paper presents an analysis of a DC-DC converter based on single phase full bridge inverter zero voltage switching (ZVS).

articleTitle: An optimum control method for active filters
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: Active filtering is the most demanding application from a control point of view compared to all the line side converter applications because many harmonics have to be controlled with minimum switching frequency. The theoretical limit of the highest order of harmonic that can be controlled is at half the switching frequency. In this paper, a new method is presented to achieve optimum performance or achieve control up to the theoretical limits. The control law is derived from the system equations. The proposed method uses differentiation in the feedforward and ways to overcome associated noise amplification problem are presented. By introducing a delay in the feedback loop, it is made sure that the feedback loop only acts when there is any error in system modeling in feed-forward path. The basic control philosophy is based on the synchronous reference frame (SRF). The proposed scheme can be easily implemented by using a digital controller for SRF based control with a fraction of additional computing power necessary to implement the proposed scheme. Both simulation and practical results are presented for a 50 kVA lab prototype.

articleTitle: Identification of motion control system using genetic algorithms
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: The soft computing has been applied to a wide variety of control systems in industry because of their control capability and flexibility. They are powerful to handle the complicated mechanical systems with nonlinearity which are difficult to model as mathematical formulas. This paper presents a novel autonomous algorithm for the identification of unknown structured mechanical systems using genetic algorithms (GA), where the optimal order of a system and the optimal set of coefficient polynomial can be determined by the optimization ability of GA.

articleTitle: Determination of thermal performance of small electric motors
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: Thermal analysis is very important for the design of low cost and long lifetime motors. This paper presents a method to analyze thermal performance of small electric motors. A finite element software is used to evaluate dynamic flux distribution and iron losses inside the motor. A computational fluid dynamics (CFD) tool is applied to estimate the temperature distribution of the motor. A double chamber calorimeter (DCC) is used to measure the induction motor losses and efficiency. Hot-spot temperatures are also measured using thermocouples. Results of tests and computation on a fractional horsepower induction motor show good agreements between theoretical estimates and measurements.

articleTitle: Mixed-mode operation of boost switch-mode rectifier
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: A mixed-mode current control at constant but two different switching frequencies for a single-phase boost type switch-mode rectifier (SMR) with single switch topology is proposed. The SMR operates in continuous input current mode (CCM) or in discontinuous input current mode (DCM) depending upon the load. This load dependent operating mode selection avoids the operation of the SMR in the dual mode, where the input current harmonic distortion is maximum. The closed loop output voltage regulation is achieved without the need of an input current sensor. The control scheme is optimized to result in an economic size of the boost inductor along with the compliance of IEC 1000-3-2 harmonic limits for input current.

articleTitle: A novel scheme of signal generating for high-resolution AC power supplies
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: A new design of high-resolution digital controlled AC source with double D/A structure is put forward in this paper. The method dealing with the problem of low D/A refresh-rate is discussed in detail. The substantial ideal of the proposal method is moving the problem in time domain into a memory space domain. With a simple algorithm and a little large size memory, the system can operate properly without increasing the clock frequency of DSP or MCU.

articleTitle: PWM high frequency inverter with soft switching for an emission control system in diesel engine
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper presents PWM high frequency inverter with soft switching, which is applied for a diesel emission control system. It is indicated that output power in the proposed inverter can be controlled according to change of the generating power of an engine, and it can be used to equip a diesel engine with the diesel emission control system. In this paper, it is shown that the proposed inverter realizes a PWM (pulse width modulation) control with soft switching at all switches.

articleTitle: Efficiency improvement on the PDP driver by using new pulse width modulated gray-level representation
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: The PDP system plays an essential role in the next generation television industry. The pixel, which inherently behaves like a lamp fabricated in the microcell, is the basic unit to compose the large PDP system. Nonlinear lighting phenomenon is exhibited. Meanwhile, high frequency switching in the MOSFET switch array is unavoidable in the PDP driver. This paper will propose new gray-level representation to enhance the electrical efficiency instead of frequency modulation. Also, efficiency enhancement will be measured to show the validity of the proposed method in this paper. It is shown that such a topology and modulation scheme will decrease the power loss obviously with respective to the traditional one.

articleTitle: A fuzzy-based control strategy for leveling electric power fluctuations in railroad substations
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper proposes a fuzzy-based control strategy for leveling electric power fluctuations in railroad substations. The power control system using an SMES (superconducting magnetic energy storage) installed in the electric railroad substation absorbs energy from the AC source line when no electric car runs and discharges energy when the railroad substation must supply high electric power to electric cars. The proposed control strategy is based on fuzzy reasoning, in which fuzzy rules are applied to the current fluctuating pattern and the energy stored in the SMES. The reduction in the rated capacity of electric installations and power loss is evaluated. The energy capacity of SMES and the scaling factor in fuzzy reasoning are discussed.

articleTitle: Predictive control of ventilating system driven by synchronous motor
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: In this paper, a novel control method-multiple feedback predictive control is developed to apply to the ventilating system of a coal mine driven by a synchronous motor. The control strategy is proposed firstly for complex ventilating system as the cascaded industrial processes divided by a computer monitor system. It breaks the traditional control method of ventilating systems and avoids the problem of modeling for the complex system. Research results indicate that the new method can solve automation control of ventilating system on a coalmine and provides stronger robustness and better performance to reject the disturbance. The predictive control to electrical drive system of the ventilating system on a coal mine can solve one kind of control problem of complex industrial objects. It is more significant for modern production and ventilating safety.

articleTitle: High power factor single-phase neutral point diode clamped rectifier
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: A control scheme for the single-phase neutral point diode clamped rectifier is proposed to achieve unity power factor, balanced neutral point voltage and constant DC bus voltage. Four power switches are used in the proposed rectifier to generate a two-level unipolar PWM or three-level PWM waveform on the rectifier terminal voltage. The hysteresis current control scheme is used to track the line current command in phase with mains voltage. To balance the neutral point voltage, a capacitor voltage compensator is employed. The effectiveness of the proposed control algorithm was verified by the computer simulations and experimental tests from a laboratory prototype.

articleTitle: The analysis of gain selection in adaptive backstepping motion control
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: Traditionally controller and estimator gains are chosen ad hoc in adaptive control designs as long as the control objectives are achieved. This paper considers motor position and velocity control problems and provides some analysis and guidelines for gain selection. Specifically we focus on an adaptive nonlinear backstepping motion control algorithm for motor position and velocity command tracking. We reformulate the nonlinear motion control system as a linear time-invariant system plus a nonlinear element in the feedback loop. By this novel reformulation some of the gains appear in the linear system. Stability and convergence rate requirements for the linear system naturally lead to the selection of these gains. By this analysis we also make the connection between the gain selection and the overall motion control system convergence rate both qualitatively and quantitatively.

articleTitle: Energy saving algorithm on induction motors controlled by a 68HC11 microcontroller system using fuzzy logic approaching
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: The potential of energy saving in induction motors is in light loads. This research has overcome the situation, by sensing the load and controlling the motor terminal voltages to meet the load requirement using a microcontroller system. The program in this microcontroller system can detect the motor load indirectly using /spl beta/ angle. Based on this angle we predict a notch angle (/spl gamma/) using a fuzzy logic algorithm. The experiment results on a squirrel cage three phase induction motor, 1.5 kW, 380/220 V, Y connected, shows that the biggest energy saved when the motor is in no load condition, is about 58%. Energy saving started at about 60% of rated load. There is no saved energy at full load condition. The fuzzy logic algorithm does work well on slow changing of loads.

articleTitle: High-power step-up converter with high efficiency and fast output voltage dynamics
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: A high-power step-up converter, which is based on the dual converter topology and is operating at a constant duty cycle, is proposed. It employs an auxiliary circuit and the output voltage is controlled with a phase-shift between two dual converters. It features a high efficiency due to the greatly reduced switch turn-off stress and a fast output voltage response with low influence of the right half-plane (RHP) zero. A 50 kHz 800 W 350 Vdc prototype with an input voltage of 20-32 Vdc has been constructed to validate this converter. The proposed converter compares favorably with the conventional pulse-width-modulated (PWM) counterpart and is considered well suited to high-power step-up applications.

articleTitle: Active power filter with neutral point switch clamped inverter
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: A shunt active power filter with neutral point switch clamped inverter is presented to eliminate nonlinear harmonic currents. The adopted neutral point switch clamped inverter is composed of two power switches and one AC power semiconductor. The voltage stress of the AC power switch is equal to half of the DC bus voltage. A neutral point voltage compensator and a variable structure control are employed in the proposed control scheme to perform neutral point voltage balance and harmonic current elimination, respectively. The proposed control scheme was verified by the computer simulations.

articleTitle: Characteristics of novel simple structured soft-switching power conversion system
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: Characteristics of both a new soft-switching power conversion system structured by a minimum number of devices and a new PWM method suitable for the power conversion system is presented. The commutation circuit for soft switching operation is inserted as an interface between a PWM converter and a PWM inverter. The number of commutations can be reduced by the PWM strategy. In the proposed system, a PWM converter and a PWM inverter are commutated once at the same time in every switching cycle by the soft-switching circuit.

articleTitle: Operational experience of using VVVF electric multiple units in Jabotabek area Indonesia
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: The Indonesian Railway Company has operated commuter trains based on variable-voltage variable-frequency (VVVF) AC traction motor drives since 1992. After an 8 year period, the total number of commuter trains that are operated is 38 train sets. This paper describes the operational experiences that have been gained during the 8 years of operation. Several measures to solve the problems encountered during that time are also described.

articleTitle: A high-current low-voltage DC power supply
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper presents new DC-DC power converter topologies that are suitable for high-current low-voltage applications. The proposed DC-DC converter consists of a cascade connection of high frequency inverter and a special rectifier topology that is suitable for low-voltage high current application. A technique to control the output voltage of the inverter with minimum switching frequency is described. Analysis of the output ripple is also presented. Simulation and experimental results are included to verify the proposed concept.

articleTitle: A novel series resonant ZCS-PFM DC-DC power converter with loosely-coupled flyback inductors
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper presents a novel topological prototype of voltage source series quasi-resonant zero current soft-switching pulse frequency modulated DC-DC power converter circuit using IGBTs which incorporates a high-frequency flyback transformer link. Its steady-state operating principle is described on the basis of simulation analysis, along with the open loop controlled power regulation characteristics of the multi-functional coupled inductors linked DC-DC power converter operating under a principle of zero current soft switching commutation.

articleTitle: On the modeling of impulse magnetizing fixture considering field and thermal characteristics
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: A capacitor discharge impulse magnetizer is used to produce a high current impulse of short duration in a impulse magnetizing fixture for magnets of the various shapes. This paper describes a method for the exact parameter estimation of an impulse magnetizer and a method for field and thermal analysis of impulse magnetizer using this parameter. As detailed field and thermal characteristics of an impulse magnetizer can be obtained, the efficient design of magnetizers which produce desired magnets will be possible using the authors' analysis procedure. As the parameter estimation method of impulse magnetizers, two different estimation methods (a method considering contact resistance and a method using an air-core test coil) are presented. Also, the temperature computation of discharging circuits of impulse magnetizers is very important since it gives some indication of the design of the magnetizing circuits. Therefore, a method for thermal analysis of an impulse magnetizer is presented.

articleTitle: A novel current-followed single-phase PFC converter
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: Two power factor correction (PFC) control techniques are presented with their respective characters in the household electrical field. Based on these, a novel control strategy is proposed in this paper with related theory and simulation analysis. A 2000 watts prototype converter is implemented to show that the experimental results are in good agreement with our theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Stability analysis of switched reluctance motor operating with fixed advance angle control scheme
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: The value of advance angle is very critical in developing motoring or braking torque in switched reluctance motor (SRM) and leads to stable or unstable operation of the drive. This paper presents a study on the effect of variation of advance angle on stability aspects of a 4 kW 8/6-pole configuration SR drive. Normally, the advance angle depends upon the motor speed and is changed with acceleration. However, in this paper, the work is conducted for stable operation of the drive for fixed advance angle control scheme. The simulated performance of SRM drive system is presented to analyze the effect of fixed value of advance angle on transient and steady state stability of the drive in terms of speed, current and torque response. The advantages of fixed advance angle control scheme are highlighted.

articleTitle: Performance of a nine-phase synchronous reluctance drive
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper describes the performance of an experimental 5 kW nine-phase synchronous reluctance motor (Syncrel) drive. Increasing the number or phases or the Syncrel above three allows the stator MMF's to be shaped, producing significantly greater torque/RMS ampere in the same volume machine. Generalized dq voltage and torque equations are derived for the nine-phase Syncrel. These demonstrate that harmonic direct and quadrature components of current contribute to torque production in the machine and can be controlled by applying appropriate stator voltages. A field-oriented controller is described and implemented using a TMS320C32 digital signal processor board. The controller designates portions of the stator winding as supplying either direct or quadrature excitation. A simple inverter switching strategy is used to control the phase currents to their reference values. An alternative control strategy based on the transformed d-q harmonic components of stator current and voltage is also presented. Experimental and simulation results are provided for both controllers.

articleTitle: Large signal analysis using discrete waveform modeling for discontinuous conduction mode boost rectifiers
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: A large signal analysis using discrete waveform modeling for discontinuous conduction mode boost rectifiers is presented in this paper. The conduction boundary of the rectifier operation is discussed. The voltage gain and the power factor are expressed as functions of the circuit parameters, including the duty ratio, switching frequency, input inductance and the load resistance. Experimental results show good conformation with the theoretical data.

articleTitle: Optimal inductance and capacitance value approximation of boost topology DC to DC converter using transient analysis
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: Conventionally, the measurement of an inductance and capacitance value of a DC-DC converter with boost topology is using linear function approach and only considerate while the switch (transistor) is in the on state. In this paper, exponential function approach is used. This function is arranged based on analyzing the converter during transient condition (i.e. the switch (transistor) is either active or inactive). The measured values of the inductance and capacitance are then compared to the simulation of the DC-DC converters and justified with an experimental result. From the comparison, it is shown that this approach is better than the conventional method.

articleTitle: A modified predictive current controller for PMSM
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: In a digital system, there are inevitable delays in calculations and applying the inverter output voltages to the motor terminals. A new predictive current controller, considering the delays, for a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) is presented. The effectiveness and feasibilities are shown by experimental results.

articleTitle: Comparing three low-switching frequency three-phase rectifiers
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: Low switching-frequency converters are a good alternative if weight and size are not a restriction. Their main features are reduced EMI emission and low switching losses. This paper performs a comparison among three low-switching frequency three-phase rectifiers. Some new important information are introduced in the paper, such as a dynamical model to design the control loop and components rating. Experimental results complete the exposition.

articleTitle: A novel automatic electronic resettable circuit for detecting and switching off failing fluorescent lamp
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: The main purpose of this study is to develop a criterion for detecting a failing fluorescent lamp with magnetic ballast and latch it to switch off condition until it is replaced. The circuit developed detects, switches off the lamp and remembers that it is faulty. On subsequent switching 'on' of the power to the circuit, the lamp does not make any attempt to start. This prevents any further high voltage appearing on the magnetic ballast to protect the ballast from failure. It prevents injection of EMI into the power lines. The novel method employed does so using nonvolatile memory in the circuit.

articleTitle: Proper topology for simple single phase inverter quasi sinusoidal which consist of combined square inverter
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: In developing countries like Indonesia it is not easy to find core material such as ferrite or thin laminate for high frequency use. The need of single phase sinusoidal inverter of 50 Hz or 400 Hz should be with some criteria cheap, easy to find raw material, simple and having fewer components. The proposed converter is based on a single phase square inverter. By making the connection of some inverters properly where the output of the secondary in series and input side of the transformer in parallel. To have minimum THD, it should have displacement conduction among the square inverter. With a displacement angle of the second inverter at 25/spl deg/ and the third one at 48/spl deg/ and pulse width conduction of 147/spl deg/ the THD could be less than 5%.

articleTitle: An on-line optimal approach to PWM-SHE gating signal generation
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: A simple and low cost method of generating the PWM specific harmonic elimination (PWM-SHE) switching signals to drive a three-phase voltage source inverter VSI is presented. This novel approach computes the switching angles online using a PC and provides the flexibility of eliminating different sets of VSI output harmonics in a quick and easy manner without any hardware change. The validity of selected PSPICE circuit result has been verified experimentally.

articleTitle: The operation of hybrid active filter for harmonic elimination
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper presents a current harmonic elimination algorithm by using the hybrid active filter. The adopted hybrid active filter consists of one active filter and one passive filter connected in series. By controlling the equivalent output voltage of active filter, the current harmonics generated from the nonlinear load are blocked and flowed into the hybrid active filter. The harmonic current detecting approach and dc link voltage regulation are proposed to obtain equivalent voltage of the active filter. The effectiveness of the proposed topology has been verified by the computer simulation and experimental results in a laboratory prototype.

articleTitle: Optimization of energy consumed by real-time applications embedded into DSP systems
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: This paper deals with consumption of real-time applications running on embedded systems. It is assumed that a significant part of the power dissipated by systems is due to input/output made between all the chips and especially between commonly used digital signal processors and their tiny internal memories and their compared to huge external memories, it is worth settling a strategy to reduce their transfers by keeping inside the processor the more interesting data that will yield to minimize the power. The authors' method is based on the modeling of C source application into two graphs, graph of data dependence and graph of expression dependence that will give information about the behavioral of data, their precise moments of utilization and the best scheduling of instructions so that data reuse is maximal. First results show that by their method it is possible to reduce by 70% the energy of some applications.

articleTitle: Modified push-pull electronic ballast for suppression of input harmonic currents
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a modified push-pull electronic ballast that can suppress input harmonic currents. The electronic ballast has partial smoothing function and charge pump function. The behavior of the proposed circuit is analyzed and experimental results are shown. The experimental results show that the circuit can decrease the harmonic distortion of the input current. It is revealed that the harmonic distortion of the input current obtained by the proposed electronic ballast satisfies the maximum limit of IEC 1000-3-2 class C sufficiently. And the electronic ballast realized the high power factor of 0.995 and the high efficiency of 0.88.

articleTitle: Integrated FPGA based ASIC design on error code correction counter for UPS telecommunication
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: The paper presents a hybrid error code correction counter suitable for the UPS telecommunication with three different signal specifications. Based on the FPGA implementation, the required functional blocks can be partitioned and designed as follows: pulse combination, serial to parallel data transfer, one frame latching, combination logic to serial pulse generation, MPU based one second pulse generation, asynchronous counter with asynchronous clear. Through systematic integration as described in this paper, the error code correction counter can be successfully designed. It is believed that the associated implementation technique will be applicable to the research and development of the tester technology on the UPS telecommunication.

articleTitle: Aspects of vector and scalar control of brushless doubly fed reluctance machines
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems. IEEE PEDS 2001 - Indonesia. Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8594)
abstract: A comprehensive comparative study of various vector control strategies for the brushless doubly fed reluctance machine (BDFRM) is presented in this paper. Open and closed-loop scalar control algorithms for the machine are developed and examined by computer simulations. Particular emphasis is placed on the machine performance/inverter size trade-offs associated with the control properties considered. Most of this analysis is carried out using normalised modelling techniques specifically focusing on the BDFRM target applications-large pump-type drives and variable speed constant frequency wind-turbine generators.
